messages:
Maya Patel: Escalation from support: p99 token latency for some customers jumped ~3x starting ~02:10 UTC. They reported streaming stalls + token bursts. Attaching their trace snippets.
Noah Reed: Any recent cache/policy deploys? I'm seeing a config rollout at 02:05 named cache-eviction-hint.v3 rolled to 15% canary.
metrics-bot: panels: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/kv/latency?from=now-4h - p95 from 320ms -> 650ms, p99 up to 1.6s. kv_prefix_cache_miss_rate rose from 0.07 -> 0.58 at 02:07.
Samira Chowdhury: That miss spike aligns. If prefix misses spike you get extra backend lookups and cache warmups per request; streaming finishes wait on token init.
Ibrahim Khan: I pulled host-level metrics for canary pool: canary-9 shows prefix_evictions/sec ~2200 and mem pressure close to 96%. Non-canary hosts in the region are <300/sec.
Jules Park: There might be a routing quirk: traffic stickiness caused a subset of customers to be routed heavily to those canary-9 hosts for ~12 minutes due to session affinity + canary fraction mismatch.
Maya Patel: Customer reports their traffic is primarily users with lots of unique prompt prefixes (multi-tenant names + dynamic metadata). High-cardinality workload.
Noah Reed: Two likely factors: 1) eviction policy change made small keys TTL aggressive -> churn, 2) key normalization bug increasing cardinality. Check logs for uppercase/lowercase model ids or extraneous whitespace.
Samira Chowdhury: I grep'd logs for cache keys around 02:05 and found many duplicate-looking keys differing only by case and a couple with trailing \"\n\" characters from older SDK versions. Example:
```
cache-key: model=TextXL:prefix=User:1234:ctx=Order-AB\n
cache-key: model=textxl:prefix=User:1234:ctx=Order-AB
```
That suggests no canonicalization before key concat. That alone could add ~18% cardinality in some flows.
Ibrahim Khan: Also found stack traces showing additional backend KV fetch of disk-backed index for misses: fetch latency median ~18ms, 99th ~210ms. Multiply that into streaming tokens and you see p99 blow up.
Noah Reed: Immediate customer mitigation options: A) revert cache-eviction-hint.v3 on canary hosts, B) move affected customer routing off canary nodes, C) temporarily increase kv-prefix pool capacity, D) enable short-lived hot-key pinning for top prefixes.
Maya Patel: We need quick action. Leaning to routing pin + capacity bump + revert if needed. Which is fastest?
Jules Park: Routing change is quick (15m) if we tag customer ids and update placement policy. Capacity bump requires infra churn but we have spare memory in that shard, so ops can bump in ~10m. Revert deploy takes ~5m.
Samira Chowdhury: I'll prepare a small prewarm job that touches top 5k observed prefixes for that customer to reduce cold misses after we revert. Script: tools/cache/prewarm.py --customer-id=CUST-449 --top-n 5000 --target hosts=canary-9.
Ibrahim Khan: Initiating remedial steps: (1) ops bump pool cap +18% on shard-9; (2) routing pin customer off canary-9 to stable host-set; (3) revert cache-eviction-hint.v3 on canary hosts.
deploy-bot: revert initiated by ibrahim: cache-eviction-hint.v3 -> previous.
metrics-bot: after revert + capacity change, miss_rate dropped from 0.58 -> 0.14 over 9 minutes. p99 trending down from 1.6s -> 410ms.
Noah Reed: Good. For a permanent fix we should: 1) canonicalize keys (lowercase + trim) at generation time, 2) revert to less aggressive eviction TTL for small keys and add LFU fallback, 3) add prewarm hook during restarts and after config rollouts, 4) fix routing/sampling so canary fraction doesn't concentrate specific customer traffic.
Samira Chowdhury: I'll open PRs for key normalization + unit tests for mixed-case keys and whitespace. Will also add a telemetry metric: cache_key_cardinality_unexpected_growth which flags >10% delta in 1m.
Maya Patel: Can you include a regression test that simulates high-cardinality prefixes and asserts miss_rate stays < 0.2 for baseline pool sizes?
Samira Chowdhury: Yes. Test plan: local sim with 250k unique prefixes over 5m with concurrency 200 against pool size X; assert miss_rate_1m < 0.2. Add to CI as integration slow-test.
Jules Park: Ops follow-ups: add automated fallback to route off canary when prefix_evictions/sec > 800 AND kv_miss_rate_1m > 0.35 for >2m. Also ensure canary traffic distribution compares customer_id distribution to baseline so one customer doesn't get concentrated allocation.
Ibrahim Khan: Note: we discovered a minor SDK issue in older client versions adding trailing newline in prompt suffix; support will notify customers to upgrade. However we must not rely on customers to fix—normalize keys server-side.
Noah Reed: Also consider cache metrics retention: increase resolution for kv-prefix metrics during rollouts so we detect spikes earlier. Add an alert: KV-Prefix-Tail-Latency-Regression. Condition: p99_stream_token_latency > 800ms AND kv_prefix_miss_rate > 0.4. Runbook: pin traffic, revert config, scale, prewarm. Drafted by me.
Maya Patel: Customer update: told them we reverted canary, increased capacity, applied hot prewarm; we're pushing a server-side fix for key normalization and will roll a safer eviction policy next week. They confirmed improved latency.
Samira Chowdhury: PR #4521 opened: key-normalize + new tests. Will request review from Noah and Maya.
Ibrahim Khan: Ops has added a temporary alert for the affected region. Also updated runbook docs with steps for routing pin and capacity bump.
metrics-bot: final snapshot at 02:40 UTC: p95=360ms, p99=420ms, kv_miss_rate=0.11, evictions/sec=240.
Maya Patel: Closing this thread once PR merged and alerting + runbook updates done. Root cause summary for postmortem: aggressive eviction TTL change in canary + routing concentration + increased cache-key cardinality due to missing normalization and SDK trailing chars. Remediation: normalization, conservative eviction heuristic (LFU + higher capacity), prewarm on rollout, routing safeguard for canaries. :white_check_mark:
